newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKS REBUFF RUSSIA FOR INTERNAL INTERFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKS REBUFF RUSSIA FOR INTERNAL INTERFERENCE.

text.p: Slovakia on Tuesday slammed Russia for interfering in its internal affairs by criticising remarks made by the a U.S. diplomat who expressed fears of Slovak foot-dragging in democratic reforms.

In an interview with the Slovak daily Pravda, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, spokesman for Russian President Boris Yeltsin, sharply criticised remarks made last month by U.S. ambassador to Slovakia Ralph Johnson that democratic reforms were too slow in coming.
But Slovak foreign ministry spokesman Ivan Korcok told journalists in Bratislava that Yastrzhembsky was out of line in making comments concerning strictly Slovak affairs.

He also criticised Yastrzhembsky for saying he regretted that "NATO pressured governments and peoples to accept this or that decision without giving the possibility to independently express their opinion".
"I would like to express my surprise that Mr Spokesman Yastrzhembsky spoke of interference by a third state into the internal affairs of Slovakia," Korcok said.
"We see no reason, and I underline that, for a second country to express itself on affairs concerning Slovakia and its external relations," he added.

In a speech in the eastern Slovak city of Presov, Johnson expressed U.S. concern that lack of progress towards democracy in Slovakia could exclude it from the first applicants for membership in western European structures.
Slovakia has already formally applied for membership in the European Union and has expressed its ambitions to join NATO, a move criticised by Russia.
"There is regrettable pressure on countries which have not yet taken a definite decision (on joining NATO)," Yastrzhembsky said in the interview published on Tuesday.
"We consider the statements by the U.S. ambassador in Presov as one of these forms of open pressure and unprecedented interference in internal affairs," he added.
Korcok, however, said there was "no need for the (Russian presidential) spokesman to have such worries".
"We see no reason for Mr Yastrzhembsky to express opinions of which we do not know whether they are or those of somebody else," he added.
Korcok underlined Slovakia's interest in good relations with Moscow and its integration into future European security systems.

"It remains an open question for us why Russia dramatises NATO expansion to the east...as Russia has had no bad experience with it," Korcok said. "Slovakia is oriented towards early NATO membership together with its neighbours."
